gaps.s: Glucose is stored in muscles and the liver as ___.

An increase in the size of the heart muscle is called ___.
A resting heart rate below 60 bpm is called ___.
Training increases ___ volume, the blood pumped per beat.

short.q: Explain why a netball player uses both aerobic and anaerobic respiration in a match.
short.model: She uses aerobic respiration for lower-intensity jogging over the whole game, and anaerobic respiration for short high-intensity sprints and jumps.
points: Aerobic for low intensity / long duration

short.q: Describe the short-term effects of exercise on heart rate and breathing rate and give a reason.
short.model: Both increase, to deliver more oxygen to the working muscles and remove carbon dioxide.
points: Both heart rate and breathing rate increase
Reason: more oxygen needed by muscles

short.q: State two factors that affect recovery time after exercise.
short.model: Fitness level and the intensity of the exercise (also cool down, age, diet).

short.q: Explain what causes fatigue in anaerobic exercise.
short.model: Without enough oxygen, glucose is broken down to lactic acid, which builds up in the muscles and causes fatigue.

short.q: Describe two long-term effects of training on the heart.
short.model: The heart gets bigger and stronger (hypertrophy), increasing stroke volume, and the resting heart rate falls (bradycardia).
